[ALUSI:92:10/r1] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | holds | God readies him for a disposition leading to hardship, such as entering Hell and its preliminaries; al-ʿusrā is formed analogously to al-yusrā.
[ALUSI:92:10/r10] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | holds | The Prophet's command to work means fulfill servanthood and the purpose of creation, while leaving hidden matters of divine lordship to God.
[ALUSI:92:10/r2] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | holds | Though taysīr derives from ease, here it means preparing and readying for what brings ease or hardship.
[ALUSI:92:10/r3] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | reports | The future particle may add emphasis or indicate the magnitude and delayed realization of the promised next-world recompense.
[ALUSI:92:10/r4] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | holds | The sequence of withholding, self-sufficiency, and denial follows the explanation already given. | mentions 92:8, 92:9
[ALUSI:92:10/r6] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | reports | One interpretation makes the outcomes obedience: God grants لطف and success toward obedience for the giver, and withdraws enabling graces so obedience becomes hardest for the miser, related to 6:125. | mentions 6:125, 92:7
[ALUSI:92:10/r7] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | reports | Another view takes al-yusrā and al-ʿusrā as the paths to Paradise and Hell and taysīr as guidance, a promise and threat concerning the afterlife. | mentions 92:7
[ALUSI:92:10/r8] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | prefers | Al-Alūsī considers it sound and near that taysīr means preparation and the outcomes are obedience and disobedience together with their good or blameworthy dispositions. | mentions 92:7
[ALUSI:92:10/r9] ALUSI, d. 1270 · علي بن أبي طالب | reports | In a report from ʿAlī, the Prophet says each person's seats in Paradise and Hell are written; when asked whether to rely on this, he commands action, saying each is made easy for the deeds suited to their created end, and recites 92:5–7. | mentions 92:5, 92:7
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | God prepares the miser for the trait leading to hardship and the Fire; yusra and ʿusra are figurative descriptions, and taysīr here means preparation.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | The future particle sa may emphasize the promise or indicate that most of the promised requital lies in the still-future afterlife.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · الإرشاد | reports | Al-Irshad explains why giving and withholding open the two clauses: each is foundational for the later belief, piety, denial, or self-sufficiency. | mentions 92:5, 92:6, 92:8, 92:9
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | One interpretation takes the first taysir as divine grace and the second as abandonment of grace, with obedience easy for the pious but difficult for others; this is linked to 6:125. | mentions 6:125
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Other readings take yusra/usra as paths to Paradise and Hell with taysir meaning guidance, or as obedience and sin and preparation for their beginnings; the latter is a sound, closely related alternative.

[ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The Prophet's instruction is to do the duties of servanthood and leave hidden divine matters to God; the descriptions apply generally despite specific occasions, since the general wording governs while those named are certainly included.
[ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r8] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | God prepares the denier for the hardest end, such as entering the Fire; he cannot overcome the hardship, which overwhelms him.
[QUTB-ZILAL:92:10/r1] QUTB-ZILAL, d. 1386 · author | holds | The rejecting person deserves to have everything made difficult: God enables hardship, denies ease, and makes each step distressing and further from right guidance.
[QUTB-ZILAL:92:10/r2] QUTB-ZILAL, d. 1386 · author | holds | Repeated stumbles can carry a person farther into misery and away from God’s approval even while that person imagines success.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r1] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | Taysīr is making something easy to obtain; its object is what is made easy, while the following lām names the beneficiary who benefits from the easing.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r10] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | One analysis reads the syntax as reversal: the person is made the object facilitated for al-yusrā or al-ʿusrā, intensifying the facilitation like the Arabic expression about presenting a she-camel to a watering-trough.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r11] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | A second analysis uses taysīr metaphorically for preparation, by the entailment between preparing something for an end and making it accessible; the lām gives purpose.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r12] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | On the preparation reading, al-yusrā and al-ʿusrā name Paradise and Hell, and the understood entry into each is hastened; making entry easy implies speed, as in Q 50:44. | mentions 50:44

2:10/r13] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | Calling the route to Hell al-ʿusrā on this reading is wordplay built on a mock-metaphor, signaled by al-ʿusrā.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r14] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | Because the prior acts of giving, piety, affirmation, miserliness, self-sufficiency, and denial precede the future facilitation, it concerns continuing and increasing those acts.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r15] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | A further permissible reading keeps taysīr literal, makes al-yusrā and al-ʿusrā descriptions of easy and difficult conditions, and understands facilitation as persistence in the deed.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r16] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · علي | reports | ʿAlī reports that at a funeral in Baqīʿ al-Gharqad the Prophet said each person's place in Paradise and Hell was written, urged them to act because each is facilitated for what they were created for, and recited this passage.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r17] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | In the hadith, a person's written place represents God's knowledge of the actual outcome, fixed without increase or decrease; it does not itself answer why people should act.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r18] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | The hadith's answer is that righteous action signals a good end; mentioning its opposite completes the comparison but is not part of that answer.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r19] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | The hadith's facilitation means preparation for good or evil deeds, unlike the verse's usage; the Prophet's recitation connects the verse to his statement as explanation and evidence.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r2] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | The complement with lām names the person for whose sake something difficult is eased and who benefits from its ease; the author compares this construction with Q 20:26 and 54:17. | mentions 20:26, 54:17
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r20] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | The hadith can show that God facilitates servants toward felicity or misery, whether in foundational faith or disbelief and in further good deeds that increase felicity or reduce misery.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r21] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | Alternatively, the recitation supports the command to act: deeds mark divine facilitation, with al-yusrā signifying felicity and al-ʿusrā misery, culminating in Paradise or the Fire.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r22] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | The passage distinguishes God's prior knowledge of human deeds from His revealed commands; a person's deeds through death indicate what God knew, while deeds remain the means to Paradise or Hell.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r23] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | Giving is singled out despite being included in piety, and miserliness despite self-sufficiency, to urge Muslims to give; these traits distinguish Muslims from polytheists.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r24] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | The verse uses combination with division and four antitheses: giving/miserliness, piety/self-sufficiency, affirming/denying, and al-yusrā/al-ʿusrā.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r3] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | Al-yusrā means what entails no hardship; its feminine form can denote a blissful condition in the Hereafter or a place.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r4] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · زيد بن أسلم ومجاهد | reports | Zayd ibn Aslam and Mujahid interpret al-yusrā as Paradise.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r5] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | The word may broadly include what benefits its possessor without hardship, namely what suits him.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r6] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | Al-ʿusrā may mean the difficult state and punishment, or Hell as the place of hardship; deeds can also be described by their eventual outcome. | mentions 74:9, 74:10
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r7] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · ابن عطية | reports | Ibn ʿAṭiyya explains facilitation as gradually involving each person in deeds of felicity or misery; deeds are called easy or hard by their eventual outcome.
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r8] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | On this reading, the future marker indicates continuing facilitation from now until life's end, as in Joseph 12:98. | mentions 12:98
[IBNASHUR:92:10/r9] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | The definite article in al-yusrā and al-ʿusrā can mark a generic class or a previously specified referent, depending on the interpretation.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Taysīr means making something easy to obtain; the direct object is what becomes easy, while the following prepositional phrase identifies the beneficiary, as in the cited verses. | mentions 20:26, 54:17
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | العسرى can denote a state of hardship or punishment, or Hell as a place of severe difficulty; the cited verse calls the Day grievous for unbelievers. | mentions 74:9, 74:10
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · ابن عطية | reports | He explains facilitation as leading people into acts of happiness or misery: righteous acts are called easy and evil acts hard according to their eventual outcome for the person.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The future marker can signal continuation from now to life's end, and the definite articles in اليسرى and العسرى may mark a kind or something already known. | mentions 12:98
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Because the syntax makes the person the one facilitated and the easy or hard outcome the beneficiary, two analyses are possible; the first preserves the literal verb through rhetorical inversion, intensifying the facilitation.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | reports | The second analysis uses تيسير figuratively for preparation and uses the لام for purpose: God prepares people for Paradise or Hell, understood as proper names, by hastening their entry; the phrase for Hell is a mocking parallel to the one for Paradise. | mentions 50:44
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Since the described acts precede the promised facilitation, it refers to continuing and increasing those established deeds.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | reports | Another reading keeps the verb literal and treats easy and difficult as descriptions of a state; facilitation means persisting in action, supported by the Bukhārī report that each person is facilitated toward the work for which they were created and the Prophet then recited these verses.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The hadith's opening statement that each person's destination was written is not the point of these verses; writing represents God's exact knowledge, and the question about whether to rely on that knowledge is answered by saying good deeds signal a good end.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The verse is connected to the Prophet's recitation as an explanation of فسنيسره: God enables a person to do works of felicity or misery, whether foundational faith or further deeds, and either sense supports divine facilitation.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | reports | Alternatively, the recitation supports the command to act: deeds mark the person's facilitation, with easy outcomes meaning felicity and Paradise and difficult outcomes meaning misery and the Fire.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The passage uses الجمع مع التقسيم and four antitheses: giving versus withholding, piety versus self-sufficiency, affirmation versus denial, and ease versus hardship.
[TABATABAI:92:8-13/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Being made ready for difficulty means being denied success in good works through their burden and an unwelcoming heart toward faith, or being prepared for punishment.
[BINTSHATI:v2p108/r2] BINTSHATI, d. 1419 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari says the paths are called easy and hard for their outcomes, or they mean the routes to Paradise and Hell.
[BINTSHATI:v2p108/r4] BINTSHATI, d. 1419 · author | holds | Usra appears in this form only in al-Layl; Quranic uses of usr and its derivatives connect hardship to the Day of Resurrection. | mentions 2:175, 65:7, 94:5-6, 54:8, 74:9, 25:26
[BINTSHATI:v2p108/r5] BINTSHATI, d. 1419 · author | rejects | The author rejects the claim that al-usra was chosen just to preserve the rhyme, and reports al-Zamakhshari's account of God's withholding help as a Mu'tazilite insinuation noted by Abu Hayyan.
[BINTSHATI:v2p109/r1] BINTSHATI, d. 1419 · author | holds | Unlike the verbal nouns usr and yusr, usra and yusra convey the extreme of hardship or ease, as do Quranic forms such as the greatest seizure and the greatest Fire. | mentions 79:25, 92:14
[BINTSHATI:v2p109/r2] BINTSHATI, d. 1419 · author | holds | Making the most difficult way easy is emphatic warning, comparable to the Quran's ironic announcement of painful punishment for hoarders and other opponents. | mentions 9:34, 4:138, 9:3, 31:7, 45:8, 3:21, 84:24
[CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1] CORPUSCORANICUM · author | holds | The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17. | mentions 92:5, 92:6, 92:7, 92:8, 92:9, 92:10, 92:11, 92:17, 92:18, 92:19, 92:20
